notes: Native Android arm64 CLI benchmark, not an APK or complete app.
Each component uses identical fixed inputs for PyTorch reference and phone runtime. Tryon uses a synthetic seeded sample and exported garment features; garment export uses posterior mean.
Decoder uses full 768x1024 output; VAE encoder is one 512x512 person tile; denoisers use native latent sizes.
Selected runs synchronize warmup/output download. Only the decoder has three selected measured repeats; other selected controls have one measured repeat.
Component latency includes inference and output download; excludes model loading, session/kernel creation, input upload, warmup and file saving.
RSS includes GPU mappings visible in the process. MNN allocator accounting omits much OpenCL/driver memory. Component peaks must not be added or treated as an end-to-end peak.
MNN INT4 quantizes Conv/MatMul weights, including more convolutions than the desktop torchao Linear-only INT4 setting. This is a separate quantization candidate.
All selected OpenCL operator output tensors report backend 3; tensor placement does not provide a kernel-level guarantee of exclusive GPU execution.
VAE ONNX Runtime CPU control closely matches PyTorch; MNN FP16/FP32, CPU and portable GroupNorm controls diverge. The responsible conversion/operator is not yet isolated.
The image-memory OpenCL VAE run was terminated under memory pressure. The initial unpatched buffer decoder crashed in ConvBufWinograd.
No full 28-step inference or full pipeline memory was measured on the phone.
